searchDocs.title: waitForServer​
searchDocs.content: </> FrameworkClient.waitForServer: boolean Determines if it should yield until server fully start.

searchDocs.title: start​
searchDocs.content: This is a yielding function. When called, it will pause the Lua thread that called the function until a result is ready to be returned, without interrupting other scripts. Yields </> FrameworkClient:start(startOptions: StartOptions) → Promise-- A promise that resolves with the time it took to start the framework. Framework:start({ components = path.to.components, controllers = path.to.controllers, handlers = path.to.handlers, }) :andThen(function(delta) print(`Client load completed. Took: {delta}s`) end) :catch(function(err) warn(`Something went wrong while starting framework from client: {err}`) end) NOTE The tag used for components will be the same as it's name, and destroy will be automatically called either when the tag is removed or the instance is destroyed. WARNING This method yields until server load completes if waitForServer is set to true. Initializes controllers, then starts controllers, then start components and finally call the handlers.

searchDocs.content: </> FrameworkServer:start(options: StartOptions) → Promise-- A promise that resolves with the time it took to start the framework. Framework:start({ components = path.to.components, handlers = path.to.handlers, services = path.to.services, }) :andThen(function(delta) print(`Server load completed. Took: {delta}s`) end) :catch(function(err) warn(`Something went wrong while starting framework from server: {err}`) end) NOTE The tag used for components will be the same as it's name, and destroy will be automatically called either when the tag is removed or the instance is destroyed. Initializes services, then starts services, then start components and finally call the handlers.
